timeline.label: RAAF press release
timeline.text: Walter Haut, public information officer of the 509th Bomb Group, writes and distributes the release announcing that Roswell Army Air Field has come into possession of a flying disc, naming Maj. Jesse Marcel Sr. as the recovering officer. Fort Worth retracts it the same day.

timeline.label: Scully's Variety columns
timeline.text: Frank Scully publishes two Variety columns describing a recovered saucer and dead occupants, sourced to Silas M. Newton and Leo A. Gebauer.

timeline.label: Behind the Flying Saucers
timeline.text: Henry Holt publishes Scully's book: a 99-foot disc, sixteen bodies, Hart Canyon near Aztec, March 1948. It becomes a bestseller and supplies the genre's narrative furniture.

timeline.label: Guy Hottel FBI memorandum
timeline.text: The special agent in charge of the FBI Washington Field Office records a third-hand account of three 50-foot circular craft recovered in New Mexico, each with three three-foot occupants in metallic cloth, attributed to high-powered radar interference. The memo closes: 'No further evaluation was attempted.'

timeline.label: Newton and Gebauer convicted
timeline.text: Scully's two sources are convicted of fraud after millionaire Herman Flader presses charges over 'doodlebug' devices sold on the claim that they used recovered alien technology.

timeline.label: Kecksburg
timeline.text: A fireball crosses eight states at about 4:44pm EST. Kecksburg residents report an object down in the woods. The Greensburg Tribune-Review reports the area 'immediately sealed off on the order of U.S. Army and State Police officials'. A later edition: 'Searchers Fail to Find Object.'

timeline.label: Minot AFB documents
timeline.text: Three Air Force documents record unexplained aerial activity around Minot AFB, North Dakota, home of the 91st Strategic Missile Wing. Published in facsimile by Robert Hastings.

timeline.label: Malmstrom Echo Flight shutdown
timeline.text: All ten Minuteman missiles of Echo Flight, 341st Strategic Missile Wing, go off alert status. An Air Force teletype the following day concerns loss of strategic alert. Robert Salas would later attribute the cause to an object over the front gate.

timeline.label: Shag Harbour
timeline.text: An object enters the water off Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia at about 11:20pm ADT before at least eleven witnesses. RCC Halifax telexes the RCAF Air Desk in Ottawa having eliminated all aircraft; the Navy tasks Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic to a three-day underwater search. Nothing is found.

timeline.label: Minot B-52 incident
timeline.text: Ground radar, base weather radar, airborne radar and visual observation converge on an object near B-52H JAG 31; the bomber's transmitter fails for four minutes; Minuteman sites of N, O, J and M Flights report alarms and an inner door combination lock moved. Blue Book sends no field investigators.

timeline.label: Loring AFB overflights begin
timeline.text: Unidentified objects are reported over the weapons storage area at Loring AFB, Maine on 27, 28 and 31 October. A Loring teletype records that an object 'demonstrated a clear intent in the weapons storage area'.

timeline.label: NMCC memorandum for the record
timeline.text: At 0253 EST Malmstrom takes seven height-finder radar cuts between 9,500 and 15,500 feet with simultaneous ground witnesses; FAA cross-tell shows no jet within 100NM; two F-106s are scrambled at 0254 and airborne at 0257; at 0344 the objects cannot be intercepted.

timeline.label: NORAD summary document
timeline.text: A NORAD document records that reliable military personnel at Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot and CFS Falconbridge had visually sighted suspicious objects during October and early November 1975.

timeline.label: CAUS FOIA request
timeline.text: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy files for the Loring, Wurtsmith and Malmstrom case files. On 6 February 1978 the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense identifies twenty-four Joint Chiefs documents; after an internal dispute Assistant Secretary Thomas Ross orders the withheld fifteen released.

timeline.label: Friedman meets Marcel
timeline.text: Stanton Friedman is put in touch with retired Lt. Col. Jesse Marcel Sr. in Baton Rouge. Marcel states the weather balloon account was a cover and that the material was not of this earth. Roswell restarts after thirty-one years.

timeline.label: Retrievals of the Third Kind
timeline.text: Leonard Stringfield delivers Status Report I at the ninth annual MUFON Symposium in Dayton, Ohio. The crash-retrieval literature begins as a research field.

timeline.label: Status Report II
timeline.text: 'The UFO Crash/Retrieval Syndrome: New Sources, New Data', published by MUFON, introduces the letter-number case coding and the first Del Rio and Wright-Patterson entries.

timeline.label: The Roswell Incident
timeline.text: Berlitz and Moore publish, combining Marcel's account with the second-hand Barney Barnett material and creating the two-site structure that no later Roswell scenario has reconciled. Haut is described in it as 'not a witness'.

timeline.label: Cash-Landrum encounter
timeline.text: Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum stop on FM 1485 near Huffman, Texas before a bright diamond-shaped object expelling flame, followed by a formation of tandem-rotor helicopters. All three report illness; Cash is hospitalised from 2 January 1981.

timeline.label: Army IG investigation
timeline.text: Lt. Col. George Sarran of the Office of the Inspector General of the US Army conducts the only thorough formal government investigation of the Cash-Landrum encounter. He finds no evidence the helicopters were US armed forces aircraft, while stating the witnesses were credible and no one appeared to be exaggerating.

timeline.label: Cash v. United States filed
timeline.text: Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum sue the United States in the Southern District of Texas under the Federal Tort Claims Act, Civil Action No. H-84-348. Peter A. Gersten is attorney in charge.

timeline.label: Clear Intent
timeline.text: Fawcett and Greenwood publish the FOIA-sourced counterweight to the anonymous-testimony literature, reproducing the NORAD, NMCC and Joint Chiefs documents on the 1975 overflights.

timeline.label: The MJ-12 film arrives
timeline.text: William L. Moore and Jaime Shandera receive an anonymous roll of undeveloped 35mm film containing the Eisenhower Briefing Document and the Truman-Forrestal memorandum. The delivery falls inside the period Moore later says he was cooperating with AFOSI.

timeline.label: Status Report IV
timeline.text: 'The Fatal Encounter at Ft. Dix-McGuire' opens with a prologue titled 'The Burden of Proof' in which Stringfield states that public research does not have proof and that affidavits, leaked documents and photographs are not proof.

timeline.label: Cash-Landrum dismissed
timeline.text: Judge Ross N. Sterling enters an Order of Dismissal under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 12(b)(1), 12(b)(6) and 56 on the United States' motion. The only US UFO personal-injury case to reach federal court ends without trial.

timeline.label: Status Report V
timeline.text: 'Is the Coverup Lid Lifting?' surveys Roswell, Aztec, Kingman, El Yunque and Brown County, Ohio, and argues that confirming a single retrieval would compel eventual sharing of alien propulsion and materials technology.

timeline.label: Moore's AFOSI admission
timeline.text: At the MUFON symposium in Las Vegas, William L. Moore states publicly that he had cooperated with Air Force Office of Special Investigations personnel from about 1980 and had knowingly passed disinformation to Paul Bennewitz.

timeline.label: UFO Crash at Roswell
timeline.text: Randle and Schmitt publish the book that drives Roswell into congressional attention. Haut, described as 'not a witness' in 1980, now appears as a witness, though not to the debris.

timeline.label: The Plains of San Agustin Controversy
timeline.text: Mark Rodeghier of CUFOS and Fred Whiting of the Fund for UFO Research publish an investigation concluding against Gerald Anderson, the only claimed first-hand witness to the second 1947 crash site. The field audits its own star witness and publishes against interest.

timeline.label: Haut's sworn affidavit
timeline.text: Walter Haut signs an affidavit stating that Col. Blanchard saw the material, that there is no chance Blanchard would have mistaken it for a weather balloon and none that Marcel would have been mistaken.

timeline.label: Status Report VII
timeline.text: 'Search for Proof in a Hall of Mirrors', Stringfield's last, opens with Walter Scott's 'I say the tale as 'twas told to me' and acknowledges the Fund for UFO Research, MUFON, CUFOS and the Mid-Ohio Research Associates. He dies ten months later.

timeline.label: Air Force report to GAO
timeline.text: Col. Richard L. Weaver, Director of Security and Special Program Oversight in the Office of the Secretary of the Air Force, and 1st Lt. James McAndrew deliver the report concluding the debris was Project Mogul. It also records that the Secretary released former airmen and contract scientists from nondisclosure obligations in writing.

timeline.label: The Roswell Report: Case Closed
timeline.text: James McAndrew publishes the bodies report through HQ USAF and the GPO. Section 2.1 works the 427th AAFBU Squadron 'M' morning reports and National Personnel Records Center holdings to show Glenn Dennis's 'Naomi Maria Selff' never existed, and identifies 1st Lt. Eileen M. Fanton as matching every other particular.

timeline.label: UFOs and the National Security State vol. I
timeline.text: Richard Dolan publishes 'Chronology of a Cover-Up, 1941-1973', moving the field's argument from witness testimony to the documented architecture of American secrecy.

timeline.label: The sealed Haut affidavit
timeline.text: Donald Schmitt composes and emails a further affidavit which Haut signs at the International UFO Museum before his daughter and a notary, embargoed until after his death. It asserts first-hand sight of a craft and bodies, contradicting his 1979, 1989 and 1993 statements.

timeline.label: Kean's FOIA request
timeline.text: Leslie Kean files with NASA for records on Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the Fragology Files 1962-1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and Cosmos 96. NASA answers 'no records' on 11 April 2003.

timeline.label: Kean v. NASA filed
timeline.text: Thirty-eight years to the day after Kecksburg, Kean sues NASA in the District of Columbia. The case is assigned to Judge Emmet G. Sullivan.

timeline.label: NASA's satellite statement
timeline.text: Before the fortieth anniversary NASA states that experts examined metallic fragments from Kecksburg and determined they came from a Soviet satellite, but that the records of those findings were lost in the 1980s. NASA's own later position is that Cosmos 96 could not have been responsible.

timeline.label: Majic Eyes Only
timeline.text: Ryan S. Wood publishes the retrieval literature's first indexed catalogue, with dates, locations, source trails and credibility weightings.

timeline.label: Court finds NASA's searches inadequate
timeline.text: Judge Sullivan holds that NASA 'has not yet met its burden of demonstrating that the search for documents was adequate', denies summary judgment in part, and orders the parties to propose search and documentation procedures creating a proper record. NASA had already admitted its first two searches were inadequate.

timeline.label: Stipulated settlement in part
timeline.text: Judge Sullivan signs the Stipulation of Settlement in Part and orders joint status reports every sixty days. NASA searches under court supervision for the next twenty-two months.

timeline.label: Kean v. NASA dismissed
timeline.text: On the parties' joint motion and NASA's representation that it had met its settlement obligations, the case is dismissed. The only federal finding of an inadequate UFO-related records search stands undisturbed.

timeline.label: UFO-Nukes Connection press conference
timeline.text: Robert Hastings convenes seven named USAF veterans at the National Press Club. CNN streams it live. Signed affidavits from Salas, Halt, McDonough, Jamison, Arneson, Fenstermacher and Nelson are on file and published in facsimile. Anonymous testimony becomes on-the-record testimony.

timeline.label: Brazilian Army inquiry on Varginha
timeline.text: The inquiry concludes the 1996 witnesses encountered Luiz Antonio de Paula, a mentally disabled man, and that the observed military vehicle movements were routine maintenance and Escola de Sargentos das Armas transport. The underlying unit movement logs are not published.

timeline.label: Friedman dies
timeline.text: Stanton Friedman dies of a heart attack at Toronto Pearson Airport returning from a lecture. He had donated his research files to the Provincial Archives of New Brunswick in the months before his death.

timeline.label: State of the record, August 2026
timeline.text: The retrieval literature stands where Stringfield left it: a large, internally consistent, unauditable testimony corpus. The nuclear-incursion strand stands materially higher, on FOIA-released NORAD, NMCC and Air Force paper plus named affiants. The only judicial findings in the domain are that a UFO injury claim fails on the pleadings and that a UFO records search was inadequate.

stringfield-status-reports.desc: The seven Status Reports are the domain's founding corpus and its founding problem. Dated and titled precisely: I, 'Retrievals of the Third Kind', MUFON Symposium, Dayton, 29 July 1978 (revised 20 July 1978), also published in Flying Saucer Review; II, 'The UFO Crash/Retrieval Syndrome: New Sources, New Data', January 1980, published by MUFON; III, 'Amassing the Evidence', 1982, endorsed by Dr. Peter Rank of Methodist Hospital and Richard H. Hall, former Assistant Director of NICAP; IV, 'The Fatal Encounter at Ft. Dix-McGuire', June 1985; V, 'Is the Coverup Lid Lifting?', January 1989; VI, 'The Inner Sanctum', July 1991, self-published at 4412 Grove Avenue, Cincinnati, edited by Richard Hall; VII, 'Search for Proof in a Hall of Mirrors', February 1994. Complete scans of all seven are public. The corpus is the reason the crash-retrieval field exists and the reason it cannot be audited: the source-protection coding that made it possible to collect made it impossible to check.

roswell-report-case-closed.desc: The most heavily documented artifact in the Roswell record, on either side. It prints the anthropomorphic dummy launch and landing locations, sworn statements from ten named Air Force personnel including Joseph W. Kittinger Jr., and full interview transcripts of the five principal pro-UFO witnesses. Its Section 2.1 nurse analysis is the only occasion on which the United States government has publicly worked a UFO witness claim down to certified daily personnel accounting records and named the individual it believes the witness actually described. Whatever one concludes about Project Mogul and the dummies, this is the standard of documentation this board holds every claim to, including the ones it finds persuasive.

kean-v-nasa.desc: The only federal court finding in existence that a US agency failed its records-search obligations on a UFO matter. Docket 1:03-cv-02509 (D.D.C.), Judge Emmet G. Sullivan, filed 9 December 2003, dismissed 24 August 2009 after a court-supervised re-search under a stipulated settlement. The opinion's most quotable line for this domain is not about UFOs at all: 'Plaintiff contends, and indeed NASA admits, that NASA's first two searches for responsive documents were inadequate.' The template - request, appeal, sue, obtain a supervised search, litigate status reports for two years - is the only method that has ever forced a US agency to look again.

sac-overflights-1975.desc: The best-documented UFO episode in United States government records, full stop. Five installations in two countries over a fortnight, logged in the NORAD Command Director's log, the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's log, National Military Command Center memoranda and base teletypes, with F-106 scrambles timed to the minute and FAA cross-tell recorded. It reached the public because two men filed a FOIA request on 26 December 1977 and an Assistant Secretary of Defense decided in February 1978 that no useful purpose would be served by withholding twenty-four Joint Chiefs documents. Nothing in the crash-retrieval literature comes within an order of magnitude of this evidentiary standard, which is precisely the point.

cash-v-united-states.desc: Civil Action No. H-84-348, S.D. Tex., Houston Division. Filed 18 January 1984 under 28 U.S.C. 1346(b) and 2671 et seq. by Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum; attorney in charge Peter A. Gersten; dismissed 21 August 1986 by Judge Ross N. Sterling under FRCP 12(b)(1), 12(b)(6) and 56. The docket sheet classifies the cause as 'Airplane Product Liability', which is the United States district court system's best available description of a UFO injury claim. The open thread is the Defense Department's internal investigation into whether the object was a US military device: it happened, and no document from it has ever surfaced.

malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.desc: The domain's cleanest illustration of the difference between an event and its explanation. That ten Minuteman missiles of Echo Flight went off alert on 16 March 1967 is Air Force paper. That an object caused it is testimony from a named officer with a signed affidavit and a corroborating letter from his own commander. That an electromagnetic pulse simulator test caused it is a competing engineering account. One unreleased document - the 341st Strategic Missile Wing unit history and crew rosters for March 1967 - would probably settle both the flight designation and the sequence, and it has not appeared in fifty-nine years.

gaps: The 341st Strategic Missile Wing unit history and launch-crew rosters for March 1967 have never been released. They would establish which flight Robert Salas was on, on which date, and what the wing recorded as the cause of the Echo Flight shutdown. Unit histories for the period are routinely declassified for other subjects.

NASA's two missing boxes of Kecksburg-era records, testified to by public liaison officer Steve McConnell in the Kean litigation, have never been located. The court-supervised search under the 16 October 2007 stipulated settlement ran for twenty-two months and did not produce them; the joint status reports themselves (docket entries 58-68) have not been examined here and may specify what was and was not found.

No document from the Defense Department's internal investigation into whether the Cash-Landrum object was a US military device has ever surfaced, although the investigation is referenced in the litigation record. The government's Motion to Dismiss and/or for Summary Judgment memorandum (docket entry filed with the motion) has not been read in the original here.

The Air Force's July 1994 report states that the Secretary of the Air Force issued an express written direction releasing former airmen and civilian contract scientists from nondisclosure obligations. That written direction is itself a document, has never been published, and appears never to have been requested under FOIA. It would establish the scope of the release and therefore what was and was not covered.

Neither Pennsylvania State Police nor US Army Corps of Engineers records of the December 1965 Kecksburg cordon have been produced by any party, despite the cordon being reported in the contemporaneous Greensburg Tribune-Review as ordered by Army and State Police officials.

Rodeghier and Whiting's 'The Plains of San Agustin Controversy' (1992) is cited at note 123 of the 1997 Air Force report and is the document that discredited Gerald Anderson from inside the field. It has not been read in the original for this board; only its conclusion as reported by the Air Force.

No AFOSI record of the relationship William L. Moore described in July 1989 - his cooperation with Air Force counterintelligence and the passing of disinformation to Paul Bennewitz - has ever been requested or released. This is the single highest-value outstanding FOIA target in the domain, because it would establish whether the MJ-12 corpus entered the record through an official channel.

Stringfield's anonymised informants are identified in his working files by letter-number code. Whether his papers survive, and whether any key mapping codes to names exists, has not been established. Without it, six of the seven Status Reports remain permanently uncheckable.

The Brazilian Army's 2010 Varginha inquiry explained the observed vehicle movements as routine maintenance and Escola de Sargentos das Armas transport but did not publish the underlying unit movement logs for 20-21 January 1996, which would either corroborate or refute the explanation.

Robert Willingham's claims about a 1950 Del Rio crash have been repeatedly restated with materially different dates, locations and claimed service roles, and his stated military record has been contested. No stable version exists to test, which is why this board carries Del Rio only as Stringfield's index entry.

The full 108-document Blue Book file set on the 24 October 1968 Minot case, and NARCAP's 141-document set, have not been read in the original here. Given that Blue Book declined to send field investigators despite SAC general officer interest, the internal routing of that decision is a documented and reachable research target.
